title: How Surfing Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how surfing works and its history. They cover the first recorded description of surfing in 1779 by Lieutenant James King aboard HMS Discovery, Hawaiian surfing as a sport of kings tied to board length and social rank, and later figures such as Mark Twain, Jack London, George Freeth and Duke Kahanamoku. They then discuss surfboard design (longboards, shortboards, fun boards, fins, rocker, rails, popouts and materials), surfing gear (leash, wax, board shorts, wetsuits, goofy foot), learning to surf (pop up, paddling out, duck dive and turtle roll), wave physics (swell formation, constructive interference, shoaling and breaking), dangers (wipeouts, riptides, reefs), surf etiquette, localism and surf gangs, and surf films and music. The episode closes with a listener mail about the Black Museum radio drama.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show with casual banter about hanging ten and Spuds Mackenzie.

segments.title: Origins and early history of surfing
segments.summary: James King's 1779 description of Hawaiian surfing aboard HMS Discovery, Polynesian and Hawaiian origins, and localism and chiefly rank in Hawaii. Board length signaled social status, and surfing was called the sport of kings.

segments.title: Mark Twain, Jack London and surfing's revival
segments.summary: Mark Twain's 1866 account in Roughing It of a failed attempt at surf bathing. Discussion of the decline and revival of Hawaiian surfing, Jack London's writing on George Freeth, and Duke Kahanamoku's swimming career.

segments.title: Surfboard evolution and fins
segments.summary: Surfboards moved from long wooden planks to shaped, lighter boards in the twentieth century. The hosts explain how fin count, toe, cant, rake, flex, base length and depth change board performance.

segments.title: Longboards, shortboards and fun boards
segments.summary: Comparison of longboards (about nine to twelve feet), shortboards, and fun boards, with notes on stability, maneuverability and rocker.

segments.title: Surfboard materials and cost
segments.summary: Wooden boards versus modern popout boards made of polyurethane or polystyrene with fiberglass and resin. Prices range from under a hundred dollars to over a thousand, and boogie boards are mentioned as an alternative.

segments.title: Surf gear: wax, leash, board shorts, wetsuits, goofy foot
segments.summary: Surf wax provides traction on the deck. The leash keeps the board attached to the ankle. Board shorts, rash guards and wetsuits are discussed, along with regular and goofy foot stances.

segments.title: How to learn to surf: paddling out and the pop up
segments.summary: Beginner steps: paddling out past the breakers, sitting in the lineup, catching a wave, the pop up, and the duck dive and turtle roll for getting past waves. Tips on patience and practice are included.

segments.title: Wave physics: formation, swell and breaking
segments.summary: Wind creates peaks that become swells. Swells combine through constructive interference, and waves break when they reach shallow water. Steep and gradual slopes make barrels or crumbling waves, and wave depth is about 1.6 times wave height.

segments.title: Surfing dangers: wipeouts and riptides
segments.summary: A cubic meter of water weighs about a metric ton. Wipeouts in hollow barrel waves are discussed, and riptides are described along with advice to swim perpendicular to the shore to escape.

segments.title: Surf etiquette, localism and surf gangs
segments.summary: The right of way goes to the surfer closest to the break. Localism and surf gangs are discussed, including the Bra Boys in Australia, San Diego gangs and the boogie board's role in rising violence. Surf films and surf music are discussed.

segments.title: Chuck's first surfing attempt and closing remarks
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Chuck's upcoming attempt at surfing and close the content portion, pointing listeners to HowStuffWorks for more on surfing.

segments.title: Listener mail: the Black Museum
segments.summary: Listener Dan from San Diego writes about the Black Museum radio drama hosted by Orson Welles, based on Scotland Yard case files, and suggests the hosts could feature it.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck give social media contact information and sign off with a Toyota tagline.
